question.worked_solution:
The number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_nC_r = \dfrac{n!}{(n-r)!r!}.
$$

Substituting $n=7$ and $r=5,$ we get

$$
\require{cancel}
	\eqalign{
                            {}_{7}C_5 &= \dfrac {7!} {(7 - 5)!5!} \[5pt]
                            &= \dfrac {7!} {2!5!} \[5pt]
                            &= \dfrac {7 \cdot 6 \cdot \cancel{5!}} {2!\cancel{5!}} \[5pt]
                            &= \dfrac {7 \cdot 6 } {2 \cdot 1 } \[5pt]
 			    & = \dfrac {42}{2} \[5pt]
                            &= 21.
	}
$$
